rules.requiredOutcome: Every retained schema migrates atomically to the current editable schema without mutating its input.
rules.currentBehavior: Schemas 1 through 8 are validated and migrated to schema 9; a failed migration publishes no partial project.

rules.requiredOutcome: The current raw project schema validates, clones, and routes as editable at the core load and migration boundary.
rules.currentBehavior: Schema 9 is the maintained writable raw-project schema and is cloned at the load boundary; this rule does not claim feature-requirement handling at the portable-archive or controller boundary.

rules.requiredOutcome: The main-process shared desktop library publishes one exact-current-schema project persistence envelope and its catalog pointer under a fenced lease without exposing filesystem paths to a renderer.
rules.currentBehavior: Metadata schema 2 binds a separate opaque library entry ID to the bounded project identity, exact schema 9, project revision, byte length, SHA-256 digest, and derived immutable revision-and-digest path. The main-only store canonicalizes the document with the bounded tagged-binary Scape codec, enforces the non-raiseable 256 MiB document ceiling, validates root schema, identity, title, and revision, writes and syncs a private stage file, atomically renames it, verifies the immutable file against the catalog descriptor, and only then publishes an exact +1 catalog revision through the fenced metadata journal. The host serializes commits, renews its lease while draining admitted work, and proves an orderly source-free Soundscaper-to-Framescaper-to-Soundscaper lease handoff with increasing fencing tokens, the same project identity, and committed-revision continuity. Full schema 9 domain validation remains an editor activation responsibility. Legacy Soundscaper project migration, managed-media publication, renderer persistence integration, orphan reclamation, packaged multi-process handoff, and per-platform parent-directory or power-loss durability remain outside this rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: Current raw project documents carry a bounded normalized declarative feature-requirements manifest, retained-schema migrations do not invent publisher declarations, maintained exact-current-schema create, load, clone, and commit paths reconcile editor-owned first-party declarations from project state, and pure evaluation classifies caller-declared availability without activating project data.
rules.currentBehavior: Schema 9 validates and deep-clones manifest schema 1, canonical feature identifiers, unique requirement IDs, closed dispositions, bounded collections and strings, and rendered-fallback descriptor source kind and digest syntax. Exact-schema-9 create, load, clone, and commit reconcile the reserved soundscaper.audio-effects bypass requirement when a maintained first-party processor exists in a non-label or non-video track, mixer group, mixer send, or master rack, and the reserved soundscaper.video-effects bypass requirement when a maintained first-party video effect exists on a timeline or Project Bin video clip. Disabled effects and inactive audio racks still declare preservation; missing or foreign effect types and video-effect stacks on non-video clips do not. An explicit publisher declaration for the same capability wins without duplication, and conflicting use of either reserved requirement ID rejects. V1-V8 migration starts from an empty publisher manifest and applies the same owned reconciliation. Evaluation reports available, unavailable, and unknown requirements while retaining the declared bypass or rendered-fallback disposition separately from the native, bypassed, or rendered-fallback effective disposition without mutating the manifest.

rules.requiredOutcome: A current-schema portable archive retains the normalized feature-requirements manifest and every fallback-only source asset, including consistent known source-reference rewriting on copy collisions.
rules.currentBehavior: Schema 9 rendered-fallback descriptors root source metadata during project and history compaction. Current-format .scape export serializes the manifest and every project source asset, import preserves the manifest and its evaluation semantics, and copy import rewrites known fallback source IDs through the same collision map as source identity. Digest integrity is governed by the route-specific current-scape-rendered-fallback-integrity rule; arbitrary future schemas remain outside this rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: Current-format, exact-current-schema .scape routes bind every rendered fallback claim to its canonical archive asset and reject a kind or digest mismatch before publication.
rules.currentBehavior: Export snapshots the admitted project root and complete source records before asynchronous asset work and serializes the same source snapshots and bounded normalized fallback manifest used for validation. Project-root and source-record accessors and callable toJSON hooks are rejected without invocation so they cannot rewrite the admitted serialization; export then hashes every emitted source body and rejects a mismatch against the completed descriptors before manifest write or destination commit. Import and inspection bind each exact-schema-9 fallback source ID, kind, and SHA-256 to the canonical manifest asset before collision lookup or storage; import then verifies the extracted asset body size and SHA-256 before source or project publication. Inspection performs descriptor binding only and does not read or hash asset bodies. Copy import rewrites the source ID while preserving the verified digest. Future schemas return and featureRequirements is not traversed. Raw-project and stored-project loads plus runtime fallback use remain outside this route-specific integrity rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: Maintained current-schema projects are evaluated against a stable selected-product capability registry before activation, and every unavailable or unregistered requirement makes the document intrinsically read-only with a per-tab compatibility report.
rules.currentBehavior: Explicit stable broad org.soundscaper.capability feature IDs map one-to-one to the capability keys in both maintained product profiles. Only a strict true profile value is available; registered non-true capabilities are unavailable and unregistered feature IDs are unknown. The controller evaluates exact schema 9 from the actual project history that will be activated before activation side effects and makes every report containing an unavailable or unknown requirement intrinsically read-only. When an existing same-ID tab wins, its stored read-only declaration also wins over the ignored incoming document's flags. The report is retained per tab, remains deeply frozen across session metadata clones, and is exposed on the document snapshot. Future schemas return no report and featureRequirements is not traversed. A separate controller-admission rule verifies declared fallback bytes; runtime fallback use remains outside this report rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: An activated exact-current-schema document with an incompatible feature report keeps a persistent structured notice associated with the active tab without activating project data or offering a compatibility override.
rules.currentBehavior: The maintained workspace consumes the active document snapshot's deeply frozen featureRequirementsCompatibility report directly. When compatible is false, it derives a separate frozen notice from only unavailable and unknown items, recomputes their counts, and persistently displays a non-dismissible localized document-level region with bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and the declared bypass or rendered-fallback disposition whenever that project tab is active. The effective disposition remains available as structured metadata rather than being mislabeled as the declaration. Available items are excluded; evaluator messages and fallback internals are not read or rendered; and the notice exposes no activation controls or claims about rendered-fallback substitution or third-party loading. Switching to a compatible or null-report tab removes the notice, and switching back restores it from that active tab's report. Future schemas produce a null report, and the workspace does not inspect their featureRequirements value. Outside the separate first-party audio- and video-effect rules, this document-level notice is not a generic affected-object placeholder, per-feature bypass control, runtime fallback selection, future-schema guarantee, or third-party activation gate.

rules.requiredOutcome: On maintained exact-current-schema activation, unavailable maintained first-party audio rack effects declared for bypass reach the editor engine only through a bounded non-persisted bypass projection while canonical state remains unchanged and every affected object stays visibly identified on its active tab.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller evaluates the authoritative actual project history and projects only exact schema 9 when its soundscaper-project report contains a registered audioEffects item that is unavailable, declares bypass, and has the effective bypassed disposition. Active, enabled, not-already-bypassed maintained processors in non-label and non-video track, mixer-group, mixer-send, and master racks become minimal bypassed engine copies; inactive racks, disabled or already-bypassed effects, and missing or foreign effect types remain untouched. Stable IDs and effect types are bounded, the lower-only production ceiling is 4,096 affected effects, overflow rejects instead of truncating, and placeholder metadata never reads or retains effect params, context, state, or other payloads. Only engine loading receives the projection: the canonical project, history, source loading, persistence, and save paths remain unchanged. Projection metadata is deeply frozen across per-tab session clones and the document snapshot. The active compatibility notice matches that metadata to one qualifying requirement and renders localized control-free affected-effect placeholders with maintained effect labels and canonical track, group, send, or master ownership without reading effect payloads. Future schemas return unchanged before rack traversal. This rule does not cover unknown or third-party effects, rendered-fallback substitution, offline render or export, per-feature activation controls, or arbitrary future schemas.

rules.requiredOutcome: On maintained exact-current-schema activation, unavailable maintained first-party video effects declared for bypass reach editor playback only through a bounded non-persisted bypass projection while canonical state remains unchanged and every affected timeline or Project Bin effect stays visibly identified on its active tab.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller evaluates the authoritative actual project history and projects only exact schema 9 when its soundscaper-project report contains a registered videoEffects item that is unavailable, declares bypass, and has the effective bypassed disposition. Enabled maintained effects on timeline and Project Bin video clips become minimal disabled activation copies; disabled effects and missing, foreign, or wrong-kind stacks remain untouched. Stable clip and effect IDs are bounded to 256 characters, effect types to 128 characters, the lower-only production ceiling is 4,096 affected effects across both locations, and overflow rejects instead of truncating. Each placeholder entry records only location, clip ID, effect ID, and effect type without reading or retaining params, context, state, or other opaque payloads. Only transient engine loading receives the project projection, and the WebGL preview filters exact affected effects from timeline stacks using trusted metadata while caching selectors and preserving unchanged stack references. The canonical project, history, source loading, persistence, save, and export or offline-render paths remain unchanged. Projection metadata is deeply frozen across per-tab session clones and the document snapshot. The active compatibility notice matches that metadata to one qualifying requirement and renders localized control-free affected-effect placeholders with maintained effect labels and canonical Timeline or Project Bin clip ownership without reading effect payloads. Future schemas return unchanged before clip or Project Bin traversal. This rule does not cover unknown or third-party effects, rendered-fallback substitution, export or offline render behavior, per-feature activation controls, arbitrary future schemas, or earlier Soundscaper project schemas.

rules.requiredOutcome: Every rendered fallback referenced by an exact-current-schema raw or stored project admitted through the maintained controller is verified against its canonical local stored bytes before activation side effects.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller verifies the authoritative exact-schema-9 activation project, including existing same-ID tab history bound by a session-owned history token. After verification it obtains one exclusive session activation reservation before project-generation invalidation, recording or engine shutdown, lock changes, ordinary engine-source loading, or normal activation persistence. The reservation rejects target history replacement, close/reopen, and competing active-project publication through synchronous session publication and is released in finally. Admission reads disable on-access PCM migration scheduling and retained-media digest claim/backfill, so verification does not publish storage maintenance. Audio claims hash the canonical audio-f32le-chunks-v1 sequence through the same checked PCM geometry and cumulative 65,536-chunk ceiling as .scape export. Video claims hash a genuine immutable original-media Blob body incrementally through the non-raiseable 4 MiB media-digest window. Unique claimed audio bytes and admitted video sizes share a non-raiseable 64 GiB cumulative ceiling before fallback body reads. Verification is sequential and cooperatively cancellable through the maintained store. Read-only video-metadata preflight is raced against cancellation, so an injected signal-ignoring provider may continue after admission rejects; a provider-stalled fallback body read can instead delay cancellation settlement and iterator cleanup. Verification deduplicates identical source claims, rejects conflicting digests before storage reads, and rejects missing, malformed, or mismatched local assets. Empty manifests and future schemas perform no asset reads, and future featureRequirements are not traversed. This admission-time rule does not verify arbitrary direct store.loadProject calls, continuously bind against later low-level source replacement, establish publisher authenticity, substitute fallback media at runtime, or provide a complete third-party activation gate.

rules.requiredOutcome: Current-format portable archive inspection evaluates maintained project feature requirements against the selected product before collision lookup, import, persistence, or activation without interpreting future project schemas.
rules.currentBehavior: The selected product is snapshotted through the shared compatibility service and injected into inspection as a provider-owned option after caller options, so a caller cannot override it. After current-format archive integrity, project-source validation, and rendered-fallback claim-to-descriptor binding, exact schema 9 is evaluated before project collision lookup and returned as a deeply frozen featureRequirementsCompatibility report. Inspection does not hash asset bodies. Future project schemas return null and featureRequirements is not traversed. This programmatic surface is the foundation for the maintained open decision; it does not use fallbacks at runtime or gate third-party activation.

rules.requiredOutcome: Every current-format, exact-current-schema archive opened through the maintained workspace/UI file routes with an incompatible selected-product feature report requires explicit compatibility-bearing consent or cancellation before import, persistence, or activation, in both collision and no-collision flows.
rules.currentBehavior: Maintained workspace/UI file-open routes use one replaceable owned request from inspection through a closed decision. A no-collision incompatible report permits only open-read-only or cancel; a combined incompatibility and ID collision permits only copy-read-only or cancel in one decision; compatible collisions permit only copy or cancel. Distinct compatibility-bearing choices fail closed against stale collision callbacks. Cancel resolves before native import, persistence, or activation. The localized dialog exposes bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and declared disposition without claiming fallback verification or runtime use; incompatible decisions default focus to Cancel and support Escape dismissal and focus restoration. Acceptance passes only the existing copy collision policy into native open, after which the controller reevaluates the actual project history and enforces it as intrinsically read-only. Future-schema null reports skip this decision. The low-level native-open API retains its caller-supplied collision policy, and it and third-party activation remain outside this rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: A raw project document with a newer schema is cloned without normalization and cannot enter a mutation or overwrite path.
rules.currentBehavior: The core migration boundary returns newer objects as structured clones with readOnly=true and reason=newer-schema.

rules.requiredOutcome: A future-schema portable archive opens read-only and can be exported unchanged without ID, storage-key, binary, or unknown-field loss.
rules.currentBehavior: The archive importer traverses known collections and may rewrite project and source identity, so arbitrary future-schema .scape round trips are not yet claimed.

rules.requiredOutcome: Designated JSON opaque extension fields survive migration, clone, save, and portable archive reopen semantically unchanged.
rules.currentBehavior: Legacy unknown JSON fields are collected under opaqueExtensions.legacyV1 and JSON-compatible opaqueExtensions survive current-schema .scape round trips.

rules.requiredOutcome: Supported Uint8Array and ArrayBuffer opaque state in exact-current-schema, current-format .scape projects uses a tagged, bounded JSON encoding and round-trips byte-exactly without activation.
rules.currentBehavior: Exact schema 9 export encodes Uint8Array values, offset-view bytes, and ArrayBuffer values with a reserved tagged descriptor under lower-only limits of 256 payloads, 4 MiB per payload, 8 MiB aggregate bytes, 100,000 traversal nodes, and depth 128; other ArrayBuffer views reject. Import and inspection validate the closed descriptor schema, unique positive IDs, canonical base64, exact byte lengths, and all limits before allocating decoded payloads, then restore the declared binary type without interpreting its bytes. Reserved-tag collisions, project-container accessors, and callable container toJSON hooks reject without invocation. Other project schemas retain ordinary JSON behavior and their tag-shaped data is not traversed.

rules.requiredOutcome: Unavailable native features remain visible and bypassable, retain editable opaque state, declare requirements, and reference an audible or visible fallback when available.
rules.currentBehavior: The schema 9 manifest, evaluator, retention roots, current-format .scape paths, selected-product controller report, and current-format .scape inspection report preserve and classify declared requirements. Maintained exact-schema-9 create, load, clone, and commit paths reconcile the owned first-party audio- and video-effects requirements. The bounded first-party audio-effect slice loads qualifying unavailable rack processors through a transient engine bypass projection, and the bounded first-party video-effect slice loads minimal disabled activation copies and filters exact affected effects from timeline stacks in WebGL preview; persistent localized control-free affected-object placeholders follow the active tab for both slices. Maintained opens provide an actionable pre-open read-only or cancel decision, the broader persistent document-level post-open report follows the active tab, and the controller still makes an activated project with an unavailable or unknown requirement intrinsically read-only. Current-format exact-schema .scape archive fallback integrity verifies the declared digest against the canonical asset, while inspection performs pre-collision descriptor binding without reading asset bodies. Maintained exact-schema-9 controller activation also verifies referenced local audio and video fallback bytes before activation side effects. The bounded current-schema .scape codec preserves supported Uint8Array and ArrayBuffer opaque native/effect state byte-exactly without activation; other buffer views remain unsupported. Generic per-object placeholders and per-feature bypass controls beyond these maintained first-party audio- and video-effect slices, rendered-fallback runtime use, and arbitrary future-schema archive preservation are not implemented.

rules.requiredOutcome: Video originals and reproducible proxies retain an explicit relationship, and proxy use never changes editorial time or original delivery semantics.
rules.currentBehavior: Video source originals are retained, but the roadmap proxy relationship and offline/relink model are not implemented.

rules.requiredOutcome: Freeze, unfreeze, commit, and rendered fallback state preserve the editable source and native-effect metadata.
rules.currentBehavior: Offline rendering exists, but no canonical freeze document state or cross-platform fallback contract is implemented.

rules.requiredOutcome: An unknown .scape container format is rejected before project or media persistence rather than guessed or partially imported.
rules.currentBehavior: The manifest parser accepts only formatVersion 1 and import staging rolls back source writes on failure.
